current: qip_edge::journal::Journal is an unbounded Vec<JournalEntry> that is never trimmed (entries are kept after shipping), hash-chained on the decision path, and drained by Cell::flush -> journal::ship -> Mirror::ship. current: qip-fabricd serves the broker library over the fabric protocol. A sequence acknowledged on each durable class (P0 control and P1 outcomes on a quorum acknowledgement, P2 journal, P3 research) is replayed byte for byte and in order by a fresh, authorised consumer after the broker restarts under a new leader epoch, and a restarted producer continues its dense stream instead of being refused. Partitions are append-only segment logs fsynced before every acknowledgement; nothing deletes a record. Backpressure is the broker's per-producer quota and lag-limit refusals (FABRIC-049).

current: qip-fabricd runs an archiver thread of its own. Each pass seals any partition's active segment that has held a batch for its stream's declared seal_age_ms (Broker::seal_aged; the segment log alone seals only by size) and archives every sealed segment of every archive-required stream through qip_storage's Archiver (Broker::archive_sealed), content-addressed and exactly once. No append waits on it: a stalled archive holds that thread inside one upload and nothing else, while a producer on a quorum acknowledgement is correctly not told its record is safe until the archive has it.

current: Every request to the broker is authenticated by bearer token against an identities file of digests and then authorised, per request, against the stream catalogue's grants (identity, stream, permission, key scope) by qip_streaming::event_fabric::{acl,service}. Produce, consume and admin are separate permissions; an own_key grant admits exactly the partition the identity's key routes to; a request no grant covers is answered AclDenied or KeyOutOfScope before it reaches the broker; an unrecognised token is a 401. qip-fabricd re-reads the catalogue while running and replaces the grants in force, so a grant added to it is honoured without a restart, and a catalogue it refuses changes nothing.

current: `qip event-fabric isolate` and `qip event-fabric release` (qip-cli) reach the broker's admin/isolate and admin/release routes. An isolation refuses every produce to that partition with Refusal::Isolated naming the operator and the reason, leaves other partitions and the partition's own retained records untouched and readable, is persisted in the broker's metadata store so a restart does not lift it, and is recorded with its release in an operator-action log under the identity whose token was verified. A request naming a different operator, or made without an admin grant, is refused.
